subject: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation

messages.author: da9a02affa1aaa26
messages.subject: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
parts:
Hi!
I would like to make interactive simulation where simulation runs N steps at a time and user could interact with it by removing/adding/changing resources. I would use shiny and reactiveTimer to make the simulation run.

Is it possible to run simulation for some steps, then change/add/remove resources and then continue running? Or do all resources have to be determined beforehand (either static or scheduled)? I am able to change e.g. resource capacity using functions and conditions based on values of selected resource, but I do not know how to take input from outside of the simulation between steps. Is this some how possible using global attributes?

messages.author: da9a02affa1aaa26
messages.subject: Re: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
parts:
To clarify my problem, I have predetermined data frame of arrival times and timeouts. At first I want to have one resource with capacity 1 and Inf queue size.
Then I want to:
1) Run simulation N steps
2) Allow user to a) add cashier, b) remove cashier
3) Run again
4) Allow change ...

I could also predermine e.g. 10 resource one of which has capasity of 1 and rest 0. Than user input would either increment one capasity from 0 to 1 (add resource) or decrease it from 1 to 0 (remove resource)

messages.author: da9a02affa1aaa26
messages.subject: Re: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
parts:
I managed to make it work. No idea if the approach is good or bad.

First I add N resources, one with capacity 1 and rest with capacity 0. I make function that checks two global variables, returns 1/2 if one of those is TRUE and 0 otherwise. It also updates the TRUE variable to FALSE. 

open <- T
close <- F

openclose <- function() {
  if (open) {
    open <<- F
    1
  } else if (close) {
    close <<- F
    2
  } else {
    0
  }
}

In trajectory I have a branch which determines using above function whether to open or close a resource

branch(
    openclose,
    c(T, T),
    trajectory() %>%
      simmer::select(function() {
        print(paste0("Opening ", res[min(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 0))]))
        get_capacity(store, res)
        res[min(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 0))]
      }) %>% 
      set_capacity_selected(1),
    trajectory() %>%
      simmer::select(function() {
        print(paste0("Closing ", res[max(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 1))]))
        res[max(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 1))]
      }) %>% 
      set_capacity_selected(0)
  )

This way user can between runs change open/close value and next arrival updates the capasities.

Sorry for the messy explanation :)

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
parts:
Hi,

Nice to know you managed to make it work. Some additional clarifications:
  • Yes, you can run the simulation for some time and then add new resources.
  • You can even add generators and change trajectories in the middle of a simulation.
  • No, you can't delete resources...
  • but you can set the capacity (and/or the queue) to zero.
  • I would argue that it's probably better to add everything you may need at the beginning, and then just play with the capacities to open/close resources.
Iñaki
